beats.narration_slice: Scientists call it involuntary musical imagery, or an earworm.
beats.visual: Vertical screen-print collage of a simplified abstract brain in three-quarter view with a bright looping ribbon of repeated geometric sound-pulses circling through it, dense black contours and cherry-red, violet, and yellow ink shapes on coarse off-white paper.
beats.purpose: introduce involuntary musical imagery as an internally repeating musical pattern
beats.visual_fingerprint: large abstract brain centered high in frame; looping pulse-ribbon enters one side, coils through the brain, and exits back toward itself; close diagram-like composition on an off-white paper field with a calm low-detail lower edge
beats.continuity: first body explanation shifts away from the opening environment into the abstract subject world

beats.narration_slice: Recent or repeated listening can trigger it.
beats.visual: Red Horned Everyman, rendered as a restrained pop-art screen-print figure, stands beside a generic tabletop speaker while identical colored pulse-shapes repeatedly stream toward his ear; several fading pulse echoes behind him imply recent listening without any notation or text.
beats.purpose: show that recent or repeated exposure to a tune can trigger an earworm
beats.visual_fingerprint: medium side-profile shot of host on the right and generic sound source on the left; repeated horizontal pulse-shapes cross the frame between them; warm orange background with sparse halftone texture and a quiet lower margin
beats.continuity: moves from the abstract definition to a concrete triggering event involving the host

beats.narration_slice: Short, distinctive fragments are easier to retrieve.
beats.visual: A bold screen-printed memory shelf holds many muted abstract shape-clusters, while one compact hot-pink and lemon-yellow zigzag fragment is being pulled forward by a simplified black hand-shaped attention cue.
beats.purpose: show that a short distinctive fragment is easier for memory to retrieve
beats.visual_fingerprint: tight frontal still-life composition of stacked abstract memory shapes; one tiny high-contrast fragment projects dramatically toward camera while the rest recede in muted rows; no character face, violet background zone
beats.continuity: changes from listening exposure to the memory-selection process that follows

beats.narration_slice: Repetition makes the next note feel predictable.
beats.visual: A diagonal staircase of repeating red-orange geometric pulse tiles climbs upward, with the final position shown as an empty outlined slot visually implied by the rhythm of the preceding shapes; no musical notation or symbols.
beats.purpose: show how repetition creates an expectation for what comes next
beats.visual_fingerprint: low-angle graphic composition with five repeating pulse blocks ascending from lower left to upper right and one anticipated empty destination at the top; lemon-yellow ground, heavy black contours, no people
beats.continuity: builds from retrieval of a fragment into the predictive pattern created by repeated structure

beats.narration_slice: Your brain can replay that pattern without any sound.
beats.visual: Red Horned Everyman sits calmly with unplugged headphones resting on a nearby table while a closed loop of vivid geometric pulses visibly circles inside a translucent graphic silhouette of his head, with no pulse connecting to any external source.
beats.purpose: show the brain internally replaying a pattern even when no sound is present
beats.visual_fingerprint: waist-up front three-quarter portrait of host in lower center; silent headphones isolated far to one side; internal violet-and-pink pulse loop enclosed entirely within the head silhouette against a cherry-red field
beats.continuity: turns the predicted sequence from the previous beat into a self-sustaining internal replay

beats.narration_slice: Idle moments give the loop room to return.
beats.visual: A lone simplified figure waits at a nearly empty bus-stop-like shelter in a wide vertical composition; most of the frame is quiet negative space while a small familiar loop of colored pulse-shapes drifts back into the upper area around the figure's head.
beats.purpose: show that unoccupied moments create space for the earworm to reappear
beats.visual_fingerprint: very wide environmental shot with tiny host silhouette low in frame, large pale warm-pink empty field above, one returning curved pulse-loop entering from upper right; sparse setting and minimal objects
beats.continuity: pulls far back from the internal close-up to show the quiet circumstances in which replay resurfaces

beats.narration_slice: Mood or personal memories can strengthen the cue.
beats.visual: An abstract memory collage radiates from a small central pulse fragment: a warm sun-like disk, a simple chair silhouette, a hand-held keepsake shape, and a soft facial-profile silhouette all connected by thick curved black pathways that brighten toward the center.
beats.purpose: show emotional state and personal memories reinforcing the cue that recalls a tune
beats.visual_fingerprint: top-down radial composition with four distinct memory objects surrounding one central repeating fragment; circular warm-orange and hot-pink forms replace the prior empty-space staging; no host body and no external sound source
beats.continuity: explains why the returning loop from an idle moment may become stronger when linked to emotion or memory

beats.narration_slice: Fighting it can keep your attention stuck on it.
beats.visual: Red Horned Everyman presses both hands against a large springy loop-shaped ribbon as if trying to push it away, but the ribbon bends back around and points toward his face; his expression stays skeptical and restrained rather than frantic.
beats.purpose: show that actively resisting the earworm can keep attention focused on it
beats.visual_fingerprint: dynamic medium-wide side view with host on left pushing against one oversized curved violet ribbon that rebounds from the right; strong diagonal tension, hot-pink background, no memory collage or sound device
beats.continuity: converts the strengthened cue into a physical metaphor for attention becoming trapped by resistance

beats.narration_slice: An absorbing task can pull attention elsewhere.
beats.visual: The host leans over a tabletop assembling a complex but readable arrangement of interlocking geometric pieces and workshop tools; his gaze is fixed on the task while the earworm ribbon is displaced to a small, faint corner shape behind him.
beats.purpose: show an engaging task redirecting attention away from the looping tune
beats.visual_fingerprint: high-angle over-the-shoulder composition focused on hands, tools, and bright interlocking shapes across a work surface; host occupies lower right while a tiny faded loop recedes at upper left; lemon-yellow and orange task zone dominates
beats.continuity: releases the direct struggle of the prior beat by redirecting the host's attention into purposeful activity

beats.narration_slice: Then the loop often fades on its own.
beats.visual: A once-bold looping ribbon of geometric pulses crosses a quiet off-white field and progressively breaks into lighter, smaller screen-print marks until only subtle registration traces remain, with the host visible as a small calm silhouette walking away at the bottom.
beats.purpose: show the earworm naturally weakening after attention has moved elsewhere
beats.visual_fingerprint: minimal long-shot composition with pulse-loop beginning large and saturated at upper left, thinning and fragmenting toward upper right; tiny departing host along the calm bottom edge; mostly off-white negative space with sparse faded ink
beats.continuity: follows the absorbing task by letting the previously displaced loop diminish without further effort
